speaker: Marge Gunderson
refusalLines: John McClane's insurance file? Personnel records are not a lending library.
And 'Frank sent me' is not an authorization level. Neither is looking disappointed.
If a document is signed with an alias, ask for the proper record. I am not identifying staff from their dramatic stationery.
I have work to do. Apparently that is the only thing anyone remembers about me today.
repeatLines: The answer is still no. The filing cabinet has not become more sociable since you last asked.

clues.label: Calendar on the laptop
clues.text: The open staff calendar marks today: 'M. Gunderson — birthday'. There is no retirement or promotion event listed.
clues.note: The occasion is today, and the entry belongs to Marge.

clues.label: Receipt tucked behind the mug
clues.text: The mug itself carries a workplace joke. A folded receipt tucked behind it lists one birthday cupcake, one candle, collection today. Customer and payer: M. Gunderson.
clues.note: Marge appears to have arranged her own birthday treat.

clues.label: Reverse of the monitor note
clues.text: On the front: 'Check for human errors (or cat hairs!)'. On the reverse, a private note: 'No cards. No birthday wishes. At least the deadlines remembered to arrive. — M.G.'
clues.note: The note says her birthday has gone unacknowledged.

options.label: She knows who altered the insurance entry

success: It is Marge's birthday and it has gone unacknowledged. Her mood is not proof that she altered the insurance record. A thoughtful birthday gesture may help start a better conversation.
hints: Talk to Marge first. Her final remark concerns being remembered today.
Inspect the laptop calendar, the mug and the note stuck to the monitor. The birthday clues are inside those close-ups, not printed on the room background.
The calendar identifies today's occasion, the receipt shows she bought her own treat, and the private note explains her mood. Choose her birthday and nobody acknowledged it.
